exact_claim: In evaluations of long-context language models performance can be position-sensitive with relevant information located in the middle of long contexts receiving less effective use in the study's evaluated tasks
source_excerpt: Performance is often highest when relevant information occurs at the beginning or end of the input context, and significantly degrades when models must access relevant information in the middle of long contexts.
study_or_product_scope: Multi-document QA and key-value retrieval across studied LLMs
approved_wording: In evaluations of long-context language models, performance can be position-sensitive, with relevant information located in the middle of long contexts receiving less effective use in the study's evaluated tasks.

exact_claim: Empirical evaluations have found that several tested models do not consistently prioritize privileged instructions when formatting conflicts or counter-framing are introduced in evaluated settings
source_excerpt: Our findings reveal that current LLMs suffer from a Control Illusion: system prompts fail to reliably constrain model behavior when conflicting instructions appear in user prompts or simulated dialogue.
study_or_product_scope: Evaluated prompt hierarchies across 6 LLM families under prompt injection/formatting clashes
approved_wording: Empirical evaluations have found that several tested models do not consistently prioritize privileged instructions when formatting conflicts or counter-framing are introduced in evaluated settings.

exact_claim: In one controlled study naïve full-broadcast synchronization increased hallucination in a multi-agent travel-planning setting while the same effect did not replicate in the study's software-planning tasks
source_excerpt: In travel planning, full broadcast increased hallucinations by 34% compared to no-sync... interestingly, in software planning tasks, the error propagation did not replicate as agents converged to low hallucination states.
study_or_product_scope: Controlled synthetic travel planning vs software task planning
approved_wording: In one controlled study, naïve full-broadcast synchronization increased hallucination in a multi-agent travel-planning setting, while the same effect did not replicate in the study's software-planning tasks.

exact_claim: Structured protocols like SEMAP organize state and report failure reductions in evaluated software engineering tasks
source_excerpt: SEMAP introduces behavioral contracts and structured communication protocols, reducing coordination failures across complex multi-turn SE benchmarks.
study_or_product_scope: Software engineering benchmark tasks evaluated in SEMAP framework
approved_wording: Structured protocols like SEMAP organize state and report failure reductions in evaluated software engineering tasks.

exact_claim: The preprint Semantic Consensus identifies Semantic Intent Divergence as a failure mode in which cooperating agents develop inconsistent interpretations of shared objectives under siloed context and absent process models
source_excerpt: We define Semantic Intent Divergence (SID) as the drift between high-level architectural specification and low-level code generation occurring under unmanaged context silos.
study_or_product_scope: 600 multi-agent workflow test runs in simulated enterprise environments
approved_wording: The preprint Semantic Consensus identifies Semantic Intent Divergence as a failure mode in which cooperating agents develop inconsistent interpretations of shared objectives under siloed context and absent process models, proposing process-aware conflict detection and governance mechanisms.

exact_claim: In a 49-task sample of SWE-bench Verified Rajan (2026) reported that 28.5% of tasks had test suites weak enough to accept a Docker-verified incorrect patch
source_excerpt: Across our audited sample of 49 SWE-bench Verified tasks, 14 tasks (28.5%) admitted candidate patches that passed all Docker-verified test suites despite leaving the core bug unresolved or introducing regressions.
study_or_product_scope: Audited subset of 49 tasks from SWE-bench Verified
approved_wording: In a 49-task sample of SWE-bench Verified, Rajan (2026) reported that 28.5% of tasks had test suites weak enough to accept a Docker-verified incorrect patch. This is a sample result, not an estimate for every coding task.

exact_claim: In a targeted audit of 138 SWE-bench Verified problems that models often failed to solve OpenAI (2026) reported material test-design or problem-description issues in 59.4% of the audited problems
source_excerpt: In our qualitative audit of 138 difficult failure instances, we identified that 82 problems (59.4%) suffered from flawed tests, ambiguous problem descriptions, or environment drift that rejected functionally valid solutions.
study_or_product_scope: 138 difficult fail problems in SWE-bench Verified
approved_wording: In a targeted audit of 138 SWE-bench Verified problems that models often failed to solve, OpenAI (2026) reported material test-design or problem-description issues in 59.4% of the audited problems. The subset was selected for difficulty; the percentage does not describe the full benchmark.

exact_claim: When an executing agent generates both test fixtures and implementation code it can produce tautological or weak assertions; practitioner reporting has documented examples of this failure mode
source_excerpt: Agents tasked with writing their own verification tests frequently author assertions that assert True or check trivial invariants rather than testing edge conditions.
study_or_product_scope: Practitioner case analysis across autonomous coding agents
approved_wording: When an executing agent generates both test fixtures and implementation code, it can produce tautological or weak assertions; practitioner reporting has documented examples of this failure mode (Autonoma, 2025).

exact_claim: In a practitioner experiment Böckeler (2024) reported that single-agent TDD loops yielded negligible mutation testing improvements because agents frequently skipped or simulated the initial failing state or tailored assertions to preexisting implementation code
source_excerpt: In our experiments with TDD in the agent loop, agents frequently skipped the red test phase or wrote tests that passed immediately without testing the intended bug.
study_or_product_scope: Practitioner experimentation with Claude and GPT-4 in coding loops
approved_wording: In a practitioner experiment, Böckeler (2024) reported that single-agent TDD loops yielded negligible mutation testing improvements because agents frequently skipped or simulated the initial failing (red) state or tailored assertions to preexisting implementation code.

exact_claim: As evaluated in STORM state-aware coordination can mediate writes made from stale observed state
source_excerpt: STORM implements state-aware dependency tracking, intercepting stale write operations and outperforming uncoordinated git-worktree baselines on Commit0-Lite and PaperBench.
approved_wording: As evaluated in STORM (Liu et al., 2026), state-aware coordination can mediate writes made from stale observed state.

exact_claim: In a production case study on multi-agent pipelines Bhaumik (2024) reported that an uncoordinated 500ms cache read triggered cascade errors across collaborating agents
source_excerpt: A 500ms cache desynchronization caused downstream agents to operate on stale risk evaluations, leading to ~20% erroneous decisions despite correct prompt instructions.
approved_wording: In a production case study on multi-agent pipelines, Bhaumik (2024) reported that an uncoordinated 500ms cache read triggered cascade errors across collaborating agents.

exact_claim: Docker Sandboxes documents a microVM-based execution model and configurable credential and network controls
source_excerpt: Docker Sandboxes provide isolated microVM environments with host-side credential mediation and customizable egress rules for running coding agents securely.
study_or_product_scope: Docker Sandboxes CLI and daemon v1.x
approved_wording: Docker Sandboxes documents a microVM-based execution model and configurable credential/network controls; organizations should validate effective policy posture at deployment time and record the applied policy digest.

exact_claim: Google Antigravity SDK provides declarative tool permission models and confirmation gates
source_excerpt: The Antigravity SDK enforces declarative tool permission policies, requiring explicit developer confirmation before executing shell commands or sensitive tools.
approved_wording: Google Antigravity SDK provides structured Pydantic schemas, sub-agent spawning, and declarative tool denial policies.

exact_claim: OpenOrchestrator provides worktree lifecycle management and pre-merge file-overlap detection
source_excerpt: owt manages ephemeral git worktrees and runs Conflict Guard to detect intersecting modified files before merge attempts.
approved_wording: OpenOrchestrator (owt) provides automated worktree lifecycle, dependency-aware write checking, and pre-merge overlap gates.

exact_claim: Mechanical controls require complete mediation and the separation of authentication from authorization
source_excerpt: Every access to every object must be checked for authority. This check is not bypassed based on previous decisions or handles.
approved_wording: Resolving a principal from a trusted issuer and authorizing that principal again at each privileged action are mechanical controls.

exact_claim: Zero Trust Architecture requires external Policy Decision Points and dynamic per-request authorization
source_excerpt: Access to individual enterprise resources is granted on a per-session basis; access is determined by dynamic policy.
approved_wording: External allow/deny policy decision points (PDP) enforce decisions at the action boundary based on dynamic policy.

exact_claim: Downstream execution actors cannot replay upstream decision records as execution authority without explicit capability issuance
source_excerpt: The authorization server must issue a security token specifically scoped to the target actor; forwarded tokens cannot be reused as ambient authority.
approved_wording: A Planning Agent may pass an allow-decision identifier but must not pass a replayable capability. The Execution Agent must authenticate as itself and obtain its own scoped capability.
